findings.location: content.body.ruleUk: "Ти і ще хтось — vosotros: Pablo y tú sois."
findings.description: The generalization omits first-person precedence. 'Someone else' can include the speaker, but tú y yo requires somos, not sois.
findings.suggestion: Specify that vosotros applies when the group includes the addressee and excludes the speaker; any group including the speaker takes first-person plural agreement.

items.reviewerAnswer: Ana → es; mi amigo → es; Ana y yo → somos; tú y yo → somos; Pablo y tú → sois; Ana y Pablo → son.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «concordancia», agreement with coordinated subjects of different grammatical persons (from memory).

findings.location: content.body.steps[id=s2].blocks[2].text: "Ти і ще хтось — vosotros: Pablo y tú sois amigos."
findings.description: The unrestricted mapping also covers tú y yo, which requires somos. The following first-person example does not explicitly resolve the overlapping rules.
findings.suggestion: State that groups containing the speaker take somos, and that sois applies to groups containing the familiar addressee but excluding the speaker.

items.reviewerAnswer: Appropriate model statements include Soy Ana, Ana es mi amiga and Somos estudiantes. Agreement must give first-person plural precedence whenever the speaker belongs to a coordinated subject.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «concordancia», agreement with coordinated subjects of different grammatical persons (from memory).

findings.location: task.errors[id=e1].feedbackUk: "Пара змішана, тому nosotros."; task.prompt[0]: "хто ви з чоловіком".
findings.description: The prompt does not specify the speaker's gender. A woman and her husband form a mixed group; a man and his husband do not. The feedback is true only under the first reading.
findings.suggestion: Clarify the speaker's gender or make the feedback independent of that unstated detail.

items.reviewerAnswer: nosotros; the group includes a man regardless of the speaker's gender.
items.notes: The accepted answer nosotros is correct under both readings; the uncertainty concerns the feedback.
sources: Packet task.prompt[0]: the companion is identified as a man, but the speaker's gender is unstated.
Review verdict instructions: use uncertain when an element would be wrong under only one of several possible readings.

findings.location: task.prompt[0]: "Тут займенники потрібні."; task.accepted[id=a2]: "Soy estudiante y él es profesor."; task.errors[id=e1].feedbackUk: "для протиставлення додаємо yo і él".
findings.description: The prompt and feedback present both pronouns as necessary, while a2 omits yo. Contrast does not categorically require an explicit first-person pronoun: soy already identifies the speaker.
findings.suggestion: Remove the claim that both pronouns are necessary, retain both accepted variants, and explain that yo may remain implicit while él identifies the other participant here.

items.reviewerAnswer: Yo soy estudiante y él es profesor. Soy estudiante y él es profesor is also natural Spanish.
sources: Course contract rule 3: consistency between task constraints and accepted answers.
RAE/ASALE, Nueva gramática de la lengua española, subject-pronoun expression and omission, including contrastive uses (from memory).

findings.location: task.prompt[0]: "Ти питаєш літню незнайому пані в банку"; task.options[id=b].outcomes: {"pron.tu-usted/context-choice":"incorrect"}.
findings.description: Age, unfamiliarity and location suggest usted but do not uniquely establish the address convention. The prompt does not explicitly require formal address; ordinary tuteo is another possible reading.
findings.suggestion: Specify that formal address is required, or allow both options with feedback explaining the respectful default and the familiar alternative.

items.reviewerAnswer: a: usted is the expected respectful default. b: tú can also fit if this interaction uses familiar address.
items.notes: The bank location does not establish whether the woman is staff or another customer, or her preferred form of address.
sources: RAE/ASALE, Diccionario panhispánico de dudas, «usted», socially conditioned use as a form of address (from memory).
Review verdict instructions: use uncertain when acceptability depends on an unspecified register or context.
